hypothesis: F changed label regime in 2023, but the existing exact-C parent and all prior supervised candidates pooled pre-break F labels. A direct binary specialist trained only on post-break F rows can learn the deployable 2025 regime; official row-local as-of histories and frozen season-start counter differences preserve row independence.

source_protocol.chronology: official train.csv row order within the completed training season
source_protocol.parent: exact-C predictions already produced without target-season labels
source_protocol.selection_rule: among no_id, pitcher_id, and their fixed 50/50 probability mean, maximize F score gain over exact-C on June-July; ties prefer no_id, then fixed_mean, then pitcher_id
source_protocol.on_fail: close without training or scoring a 2024 specialist
source_protocol.on_pass: write an immutable selected-recipe lock and implementation hash before the 2024 run

features.base: all official pre-pitch train columns except row_id, control_success, season, and constant game_type
derived_row_local: log1p official pitcher and batter counts
current-season pitcher success count and smoothed rate reconstructed exactly from the row and frozen prior-season end state
current-season batter success count and smoothed rate reconstructed exactly in the same way
the official row-local reverse, middle, recent-game, and pitchmix rates remain available as raw inputs; no non-reconstructible final prior-season component label is invented
features.frozen_prior: mean control_success of completed post-break F fit rows only

views.no_id: base and derived features with pitcher_id and batter_id removed
views.pitcher_id: no_id plus pitcher_id as a categorical feature

confirmation_2024.full_candidate: selected F specialist on F rows; exact-C unchanged on R rows

complexity.deployed_components: two for a selected single view, or three for fixed_mean, including the unchanged exact-C R route
